page: Amazon Web Services g4dn.xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the Nitro System, designed primarily for machine learning inference and graphics-intensive applications. It is powered by a custom Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 2.5 GHz across 4 vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with hyperthreading. The host system supplies 16 GB of DDR4 system memory clocked at 3 GHz, matched with 125 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

The primary computational engine of the g4dn.xlarge is a single NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture, providing 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Benchmark results reflect a stark performance bifurcation between host CPU execution and hardware-accelerated processing. Conventional CPU and system memory metrics place this instance in the lower quartile, with low multi-threaded decompression, compression, and general integer throughput scores on Geekbench and PassMark. Conversely, GPU acceleration delivers top-tier results in small and medium large language model prompt evaluation, exceeding 8,400 tokens per second on 135M models and over 1,170 tokens per second on 7B models, alongside strong text generation throughput.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the instance balances entry-level host compute with hardware-accelerated inferencing. Bundled high-speed local NVMe storage reduces scratch disk bottlenecks, while the modest vCPU allocation avoids resource waste when workloads are predominantly GPU-bound. Workloads requiring intensive general-purpose CPU processing or excessive host memory will encounter clear performance limits, but the configuration fits deep learning inference, lightweight model fine-tuning, video transcoding, and remote graphics rendering.
description: Amazon Web Services g4dn.xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered for GPU-driven workloads such as machine learning inference and visual computing. Powered by the Nitro hypervisor, it features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 4 vCPUs, 16 GB of DDR4 system memory, a 125 GB local NVMe SSD, and 5 Gbps baseline networking. Acceleration is delivered via a dedicated NVIDIA T4 GPU equipped with 16 GB of VRAM. While host-level CPU and memory benchmarks fall into lower performance tiers on general computing suites, the instance exhibits top-tier inference speeds for small and medium language models, delivering over 1,170 prompt tokens per second on 7B parameters. This hardware profile provides a resource-balanced platform for real-time model inference, lightweight graphics rendering, and video processing, where GPU throughput supersedes raw host CPU compute.
